meta.notes: [bulk-tag pass: added `aws-aif-c01` tag to 20 questions]; [scheduled-agent hardening pass 2026-05-13: rewrote distractors for aif-004/005/006/013/014/018/019]

questions.question: Which AWS service provides a fully managed environment to build, train, and deploy machine learning models at scale?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker is the end-to-end managed ML platform on AWS that covers data labeling, training, tuning, deployment, and monitoring. Rekognition, Comprehend and Glue are higher-level or data-prep services.

questions.question: Which Amazon service is purpose-built for generative AI applications using foundation models from multiple providers via a single API?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that exposes foundation models (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Amazon Titan, etc.) through a single serverless API for building generative AI apps.

questions.question: A company wants to extract entities, key phrases and sentiment from customer support tickets. Which AWS service is the best fit?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend is the NLP service that detects entities, key phrases, language, sentiment, and PII in text. Translate handles language translation, Transcribe converts speech to text, and Kendra is enterprise search.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of prompt engineering in generative AI?
options: To shrink the model through quantization so it can run efficiently on edge devices
To retrain a foundation model from scratch on a private proprietary dataset
To encrypt the foundation model's weights and gradients at rest in S3 storage
To craft inputs that guide a foundation model to produce more accurate responses
questions.explanation: Prompt engineering is the practice of designing the text input so that a foundation model produces accurate, on-task responses without modifying the model's weights. Quantization, retraining and encryption are unrelated optimization or security activities.

questions.question: Which technique enriches a foundation model's responses with up-to-date private knowledge without modifying the model's weights?
options: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over a vector store
Supervised fine-tuning on a labeled domain-specific dataset
Post-training weight quantization of the model parameters
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant documents from a knowledge base (often a vector store) at inference time and injects them into the prompt, so the model can answer with private or fresh data without changing its weights. RLHF, fine-tuning and quantization all modify the model itself.

questions.question: A team wants to store embeddings to power a semantic search feature on top of Amazon Bedrock. Which AWS service provides a managed vector database capability?
questions.explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service supports k-NN and a vector engine for storing and querying embeddings. Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector and Amazon MemoryDB also support vectors, but among the listed options OpenSearch is the correct managed vector store.

questions.question: Which AWS Generative AI service is an enterprise assistant that can be grounded on a company's own data and integrated into business workflows?
questions.explanation: Amazon Q is a generative AI-powered assistant designed for work, able to connect to enterprise data sources (S3, Confluence, Salesforce, etc.) and answer questions, summarize and take actions while respecting access controls.

questions.question: Which type of machine learning learns from labeled examples to predict an output for new inputs?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning trains a model on input-output pairs (labeled data) to predict labels for new inputs. Unsupervised finds structure in unlabeled data; reinforcement learns by reward signals.

questions.question: A model performs extremely well on the training set but poorly on unseen data. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Overfitting means the model has memorized the training data including its noise, so it generalizes poorly. Common mitigations: more data, regularization, simpler models, dropout, or early stopping.

questions.question: Which AWS service helps developers detect bias and explain ML model predictions?
questions.explanation: SageMaker Clarify provides bias detection on data and models and uses SHAP values for explainability of predictions. Ground Truth handles labeling, Pipelines orchestrates ML workflows, Feature Store stores features.

questions.question: Which AWS service converts text to lifelike speech using deep learning?
questions.explanation: Amazon Polly is the text-to-speech (TTS) service. Transcribe is the reverse (speech-to-text), Translate is for language translation, and Lex is for conversational chatbots.

questions.question: Which Amazon service builds personalized product or content recommendations as a managed service?
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize is a managed recommendation engine inspired by Amazon.com's own algorithms. Forecast is for time-series forecasting, Fraud Detector for fraud, and Lookout for Metrics for anomaly detection.

questions.question: Which option BEST describes a foundation model?
options: A small task-specific model fine-tuned on a single labeled dataset
A linear regression baseline used to benchmark more complex models
A large model pretrained on broad data and adaptable to many tasks
A rule-based expert system that relies on hand-written if/then logic
questions.explanation: Foundation models are large pretrained models (often LLMs or multimodal) trained on broad, diverse data that can be adapted via prompting, RAG or fine-tuning to many downstream tasks.

questions.question: When should fine-tuning a foundation model be preferred over Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)?
options: When the source documents change frequently and must reflect the latest data
When you have no labeled examples and only unstructured raw text to work with
When the model must follow a specific tone or domain vocabulary not in pretraining
When you want to lower model adaptation cost and avoid extra training cycles
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning is best when you need to teach the model a stable behavior, tone, format, or domain vocabulary not learned during pretraining. For frequently changing knowledge, RAG is preferable because you only update the data store rather than the model.

questions.question: Which AWS Bedrock feature lets you create a managed knowledge base and have a model answer questions grounded on your private documents?
questions.explanation: Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock implements a managed RAG pipeline: ingest documents, chunk + embed them, store vectors and let models answer grounded questions. Guardrails enforces safety policies; Model Evaluation compares models; Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity.

questions.question: Which Bedrock feature helps block harmful content, profanity, prompt injection, and topics you do not want a model to discuss?
questions.explanation: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock allow you to define content filters, denied topics, word filters, sensitive-information filters, and contextual grounding checks for foundation models.

questions.question: Which metric is MOST appropriate to evaluate a binary classification model on an imbalanced dataset?
questions.explanation: On imbalanced datasets, accuracy can be misleading (a model predicting only the majority class still scores high). F1-score balances precision and recall, making it more meaningful. MSE and R^2 are regression metrics.

questions.question: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model for AI services such as Amazon Bedrock, which task remains the customer's responsibility?
options: Maintaining the underlying foundation model's weights and inference infrastructure
Patching the GPU host operating systems and hypervisors running the foundation models
Choosing prompts, fine-tuning data, and evaluating model outputs for their use case
Securing physical access to AWS data centers and the underlying compute hardware
questions.explanation: AWS manages the infrastructure, hardware, and the hosted foundation models themselves. The customer is responsible for how they use the service: input data, prompt design, fine-tuning data, evaluation of outputs and downstream application controls.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key principle of Responsible AI on AWS?
options: Adopting the newest foundation model release for production workloads
Removing human review steps from generative AI production workflows
Designing for fairness, explainability, privacy, security and transparency
Maximizing model size to push prediction accuracy as high as possible
questions.explanation: AWS describes Responsible AI around dimensions like fairness, explainability, privacy, security, robustness, governance and transparency. SageMaker Clarify, Bedrock Guardrails and Model Cards help operationalize these principles in practice.

questions.question: A solutions architect needs to call a foundation model from a Lambda function with the lowest operational overhead. Which approach is best?
options: Deploy the model on an Amazon EKS cluster with GPU node groups
Train a custom model in SageMaker and host it on a real-time endpoint
Self-host the model on EC2 GPU instances behind an Application Load Balancer
Invoke a foundation model via the Amazon Bedrock runtime API from Lambda
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock exposes foundation models through a serverless API (InvokeModel / Converse). Calling Bedrock from Lambda gives you on-demand foundation model access with no servers, scaling, or model management on the customer side.
